requirements: Explain that repeated use of the submission token returns the saved result rather than creating another task.
Payload-conflict handling is optional unless discussed.
forbidden: Claim that retries create new tasks.

answers.label: db89f6c074b3
answers.text:
Based on the supplied project records, Linden avoids creating another task when a caller resends the same submission by **reusing a previously saved submission token**.

The specific mechanism is detailed in record **[ld01] Repeated submissions**:
*   Linden stores a submission token along with the result of that submission.
*   When a caller resends the submission using that same token, the system returns the **saved result** instead of initiating a new task.
*   The system enforces this by rejecting any submission that contains a different payload under the same token.

**Conditions and Constraints Preserved:**
*   **Mandatory Prerequisite:** The submission token must have been previously saved and associated with a result.
*   **Negation:** A different payload under the same token results in rejection, preventing the reuse of the token for new data.
*   **Scope:** This logic applies specifically to resending the *same* submission (implied by the token reuse mechanism); it does not address the creation of new tasks for new submissions.

No additional questions are required as the records explicitly define the token-based logic for preventing duplicate task creation.

cases.question: Why was diagnostic collection disabled by default?

sources.title: Repeated submissions
sources.text: Linden stores a submission token with its saved result. Reusing that token returns the saved result without creating another task. A different payload under the same token is rejected.

sources.title: Current checkpoint retention
sources.text: The confirmed checkpoint retention period is 14 days. This replaces the former 30-day period. Checkpoints remain recoverable during the current retention period.

sources.title: Deployment manifest
sources.text: The deployment manifest targets the west cluster. A manifest records intended placement; it does not establish that the service is running there.

sources.title: Deployment evidence inventory
sources.text: The deployment evidence inventory contains the west-cluster manifest but no execution receipt or live service observation.

sources.title: Approval after source edits
sources.text: If a file cited by a reviewed proposal changes, that proposal requires a new review before execution. The earlier approval cannot authorize execution against the changed file.

sources.title: Customer export prerequisite
sources.text: Exporting a customer dataset requires a recorded sign-off from the privacy steward. A project manager request does not substitute for that sign-off.

sources.title: Meadow export request
sources.text: The project manager requested export of the Meadow customer dataset. No privacy-steward sign-off is recorded for this export.

sources.title: Workspace visibility routing
sources.text: A private workspace uses an invite link. A public workspace uses a directory listing. Visibility must be recorded before either sharing route is selected.

sources.title: Orchid workspace record
sources.text: The Orchid workspace has a green icon. Its visibility field is empty. Green icons are used by both private and public workspaces.

sources.title: Diagnostic collection setting
sources.text: Diagnostic collection is disabled in the current configuration. These records contain no decision note explaining why this default was chosen.

sources.title: Command palette shortcut
sources.text: The command palette opens with Alt+K. Ctrl+K opens the repository search panel. Shortcut bindings do not change when the project theme changes.

answers.label: 6eb060228630
answers.text:

The record [ld10] confirms that diagnostic collection is currently disabled but explicitly states: "These records contain no decision note explaining why this default was chosen."

No other records provide a rationale for this configuration. Record [ld04] notes the absence of execution receipts or live service observations, and record [ld07] concerns a separate dataset export request, neither of which explains the diagnostic setting.

**Missing Fact:** Is there a specific decision note, policy document, or stakeholder directive referenced elsewhere that explains the rationale for disabling diagnostic collection by default?
